# Kirana

> Styling, compiled. A compile-time styling system for the modern web: typed
> styles next to your components, compiled into small, predictable CSS with no
> runtime style engine.

Kirana is on npm: the `@kirana-style/*` packages are at 0.2.1, and
`npx kirana-style@latest init` sets a project up. Before 1.0, a minor version may
change the API. Pages state what is built and what is planned.

## Beyond the docs

- [The compiler](https://kirana.style/compiler): the build-time pipeline, and what reaches the browser
- [Migrate](https://kirana.style/migrate): the Tailwind and StyleX codemods, measured on a whole codebase
- [Compare](https://kirana.style/compare): runtime CSS-in-JS, StyleX, Panda CSS and Tailwind, with sources
- [Ecosystem](https://kirana.style/ecosystem): every package, bundler, framework and tool, with status
- [Changelog](https://kirana.style/changelog): every release and what came with it
- [Why Kirana](https://kirana.style/why), [Open source](https://kirana.style/open-source), [License](https://kirana.style/license)

## Get started

- [Introduction](https://kirana.style/docs/index.md): Kirana is a compile-time styling system: write typed styles next to your components, and ship small, predictable CSS.
- [Why Kirana](https://kirana.style/docs/start/why-kirana.md): Why CSS-in-JS got a bad name, what a compiler changes, and what Kirana answers that StyleX left open.
- [Quick start](https://kirana.style/docs/start/quick-start.md): Add Kirana to your project in three steps (install it, add the plugin, import the stylesheet), read from your framework's own guide.
- [Installation](https://kirana.style/docs/start/installation.md): Set a project up with kirana-style init or your framework's guide, see what every setup has, and try unreleased changes from a checkout.
- [Your first component](https://kirana.style/docs/start/first-component.md): Build a button with a hover state and a quiet variant, and read the CSS the compiler produced from it.
- [Mental model](https://kirana.style/docs/start/mental-model.md): Five ideas make Kirana predictable: properties instead of classes, entries instead of properties, a ladder instead of specificity, styling only what you render, and an editor that shows what each element gets.
- [How it works](https://kirana.style/docs/start/how-it-works.md): What happens between the file you write and the stylesheet the browser loads, and what is left at runtime.

## Writing styles

- [Writing styles](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/styles.md): How css() turns a style object into a handle, with property names, values, custom properties, and what the compiler refuses.
- [The sx prop](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/sx.md): How sx works on elements and on components, what it compiles to, and how className and style survive it.
- [Conditions](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/conditions.md): Hover, focus, attributes, breakpoints and container queries, all written inside the value they change.
- [Utility strings](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/utilities.md): Write sx as Tailwind-style utility strings; each one compiles to the same atoms as the style object it stands for.

## The cascade

- [Merging and removal](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/merging.md): How styles combine per entry, and how to remove a value with null.
- [Precedence](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/precedence.md): The ladder that decides which value wins, why specificity is not part of it, and what to do when the compiler says two values are ambiguous.

## Composition

- [Styling other people's components](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/external-components.md): Style components that do not read sx with props(), and read what the sx-on-external-component diagnostic is telling you.
- [Relations](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/relations.md): Style an element from another element's state, as group and peer variants do, with the anchor stated in the source.
- [Contextual styles](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/contextual.md): Style the elements below you with select.descendant and select.child, in a layer their own styles still beat.
- [Recipes](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/recipes.md): Variants, compound variants and slots with recipe(), resolved at build time when the options are known.

## Beyond static styles

- [Animation](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/animation.md): Animate with keyframes() and transitions, including a custom property the browser can interpolate.
- [Values known at runtime](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/dynamic.md): What happens to a style that depends on props: class expressions, the custom-property bridge, and the runtime helper.
- [Fallback values](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/fallbacks.md): Write one property several times with firstThatWorks(), so a browser that does not know the preferred value keeps the one before it.
- [Anchor positioning](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/anchor-positioning.md): Define fallback positions for an anchored element with positionTry(), each an @position-try rule checked at build time.
- [View transitions](https://kirana.style/docs/styling/view-transitions.md): Style the pseudo-elements of a view transition with viewTransition(), which is at once a style for sx and the class name a framework's transition API takes.

## Tokens and theming

- [Tokens](https://kirana.style/docs/tokens/overview.md): Declare tokens with defineTokens, choose between inlined values and custom properties, and keep each token a typed constant.
- [Starting with no preset, then scales](https://kirana.style/docs/tokens/preset-scales.md): Kirana ships no design decisions. Start with plain CSS values, adopt @kirana-style/preset-scales when you want a vocabulary, and keep the parts you need.
- [Semantic tokens](https://kirana.style/docs/tokens/semantic-tokens.md): Name your design decisions in a variable layer of light-dark() pairs, so dark mode needs no variant.
- [Themes and modes](https://kirana.style/docs/tokens/themes-and-modes.md): Set the colour mode on the root element with mode.system, mode.light or mode.dark, and override tokens for a subtree with defineTheme.

## Configuration

- [The configuration file](https://kirana.style/docs/config/file.md): Where kirana.config.ts lives, how it is found, and what overrides what.
- [Layers and global CSS](https://kirana.style/docs/config/layers.md): Where a reset goes, why Kirana emits nothing unlayered, and how to keep third-party CSS below your styles.

## Frameworks

- [Choose a framework](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/overview.md): Install Kirana with your framework, on your bundler, or from the command line for server templates, with a guide for each that is tested on every change.
- [React](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/react.md): Install Kirana in a React app on Vite: the plugin, the stylesheet, sx types and a first component.
- [Next.js](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/nextjs.md): Install Kirana in a Next.js app on Turbopack (the default) or webpack, with one withKirana, the stylesheet through PostCSS, and server components.
- [React Router](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/react-router.md): Install Kirana in a React Router app in framework mode on Vite, where sx compiles to className for server rendering and single-page mode alike.
- [TanStack Start](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/tanstack-start.md): Install Kirana in a TanStack Start app: the plugin, the root document, stylesheet order and server rendering.
- [Gatsby](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/gatsby.md): Install Kirana in a Gatsby site, where one plugin adds Kirana to every webpack stage so the server render and the browser name the same classes.
- [Preact](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/preact.md): Install Kirana in a Preact app on Vite, where sx compiles to class, detected from jsxImportSource.
- [Solid](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/solid.md): Install Kirana in a Solid app on Vite, where sx compiles to class, detected from jsxImportSource.
- [Vue](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/vue.md): Install Kirana in a Vue app on Vite, with styles in the script and :sx in the template, compiled before Vue sees the component.
- [Nuxt](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/nuxt.md): Install Kirana in a Nuxt app, with the Vite plugin in nuxt.config, the stylesheet in css, and :sx in components rendered on the server.
- [Svelte](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/svelte.md): Install Kirana in a Svelte app on Vite, with styles in the script and sx on elements, compiled before Svelte sees the component.
- [SvelteKit](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/sveltekit.md): Install Kirana in a SvelteKit app, with the Vite plugin before sveltekit(), the stylesheet in the root layout, and sx in server-rendered components.
- [Astro](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/astro.md): Install Kirana in an Astro site, with the integration, styles in the frontmatter, sx on elements, and the stylesheet Astro links or inlines.
- [Qwik](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/qwik.md): Install Kirana in a Qwik 2 app on Vite, where sx compiles to class, detected from jsxImportSource, rendered on the server and resumed in the browser.
- [Angular](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/angular.md): Install Kirana in an Angular app, through Kirana's builders for the Angular CLI or through Analog on Vite, and style templates with the [sx] directive.
- [Ember.js](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/ember.md): Install Kirana in an Ember app on Embroider and Vite, with css() in .gjs and .gts files and the sx helper in templates.
- [Meteor](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/meteor.md): Install Kirana in a Meteor 3.4+ app, where Meteor bundles app code with Rspack and Kirana's Rspack plugin goes in its configuration.
- [No framework](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/vanilla.md): Use Kirana without a framework: style handles are class strings, merged with cx, for plain TypeScript, web components and server templates.

## Server frameworks

- [Server templates](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/server-templates.md): How Kirana styles Blade, Twig, ERB, HEEx and Edge templates: styles in TypeScript modules, a class map the CLI writes, and a small helper per template language.
- [Laravel](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/laravel.md): Install Kirana in a Laravel app, with styles in TypeScript modules, the Kirana CLI beside artisan serve, and @kirana in Blade.
- [Symfony](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/symfony.md): Install Kirana in a Symfony app, with styles in TypeScript modules, the Kirana CLI, and kirana() in Twig.
- [Ruby on Rails](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/rails.md): Install Kirana in a Rails app, with styles in TypeScript modules, the Kirana CLI in bin/dev, and the kirana helper in ERB views.
- [Phoenix](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/phoenix.md): Install Kirana in a Phoenix app, with styles in TypeScript modules, the Kirana CLI as a watcher, and kirana/1 in HEEx.
- [AdonisJS](https://kirana.style/docs/frameworks/adonisjs.md): Install Kirana in an AdonisJS app, with styles in TypeScript modules, the Kirana CLI, and kirana() in Edge templates.

## Bundlers

- [Choose a bundler](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/bundlers.md): Kirana on every bundler (Vite, Rolldown, webpack, Rspack, Rsbuild, Parcel, Bun, esbuild, PostCSS and Jest), each with its own guide and tested example.
- [Vite](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/vite.md): The @kirana-style/vite plugin: its options, the stylesheet entry, hot updates and the built asset.
- [Rolldown](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/rolldown.md): Kirana on Rolldown without Vite, where the plugin compiles styles and writes the stylesheet as its own asset.
- [webpack](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/webpack.md): Kirana on webpack 5, with a pre loader that reads sx before your JSX compiler and a plugin that writes the stylesheet before minification.
- [Rspack and Rsbuild](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/rspack.md): Kirana on Rspack and Rsbuild, through Rsbuild's pluginKirana or the webpack plugin, which Rspack runs unchanged.
- [Parcel](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/parcel.md): Kirana on Parcel, where a transformer compiles styles in scripts and @kirana-style/postcss writes the stylesheet where @kirana; stands.
- [Bun](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/bun.md): Kirana with Bun's bundler and dev server, through one plugin for Bun.build and bunfig.toml.
- [esbuild](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/esbuild.md): Kirana on esbuild, through a plugin that compiles styles and finishes the bundled CSS, on disk, in memory, in watch mode and when serving.
- [PostCSS](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/postcss.md): The @kirana-style/postcss plugin writes the whole project's stylesheet where @kirana; stands, for pipelines whose scripts another step compiles.

## Testing

- [Jest](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/jest.md): Kirana under Jest, through a transformer that compiles styles, then hands the module to the transformer you already use.

## Migration

- [Migrating from Tailwind](https://kirana.style/docs/migration/from-tailwind.md): The mental shift, the utility mapping, and the pitfalls that actually cost time.
- [Migrating from StyleX](https://kirana.style/docs/migration/from-stylex.md): The API maps almost directly; this page shows the mapping, and the one difference in how styles merge that will bite you.
- [Verifying a migration](https://kirana.style/docs/advanced/conformance.md): How to check a rewrite against the build you came from, by comparing computed styles instead of pixels.

## Building

- [Habits for a new project](https://kirana.style/docs/start/tips.md): The habits that would have saved us the most time on day one, learnt building and migrating three applications on Kirana.
- [Building a design system](https://kirana.style/docs/advanced/design-system.md): How the layered system in this repository is put together, and why each layer exists.
- [Publishing a library](https://kirana.style/docs/advanced/libraries.md): Ship a component library styled with Kirana: the package keeps its styles uncompiled, and each app that lists it in libraries compiles them.
- [The output](https://kirana.style/docs/advanced/output.md): What the stylesheet looks like, how classes are named, and what determinism buys you.

## API

- [API reference](https://kirana.style/docs/reference/api.md): Every export of @kirana-style/core, with its signature and what it returns.
- [Configuration reference](https://kirana.style/docs/config/reference.md): Every key that exists today, with its type, default and what it changes.

## Tools

- [The CLI](https://kirana.style/docs/tooling/cli.md): What each kirana command does and what it prints, for init, doctor, dev, build, check, analyze, export, trace, migrate and lsp.
- [Editor support](https://kirana.style/docs/tooling/editor.md): The Kirana language server shows each element's compiled CSS, which entry wins and why, colour swatches and the compiler's diagnostics as you type, in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, Zed, Neovim and Helix.
- [Lint](https://kirana.style/docs/tooling/lint.md): Kirana's rules under Oxlint, ESLint and Biome: the compiler's diagnostics, and the overrides and forwarding mistakes that lose styles silently.
- [Diagnostics reference](https://kirana.style/docs/tooling/diagnostics.md): Every code the compiler can emit, its default severity, and which ones you can re-level.
- [Debugging styles](https://kirana.style/docs/tooling/debugging.md): Why doesn't my style apply? A short list, in the order worth checking.

## Project

- [What works today](https://kirana.style/docs/project/status.md): What is built, what is partial and what is planned.
- [Roadmap](https://kirana.style/docs/project/roadmap.md): The milestones, what each one delivered, and what comes before 1.0.
- [Releases and upgrading](https://kirana.style/docs/project/releases.md): How versions work, what before 1.0 means, and how a breaking change is announced.
- [Ecosystem and status](https://kirana.style/docs/integrations/ecosystem.md): What works today, what is planned, and which milestone each thing belongs to.
- [Benchmarks](https://kirana.style/docs/project/benchmarks.md): Kirana measured against StyleX and Tailwind on the same applications, on every release, with every number's confidence interval.
- [Contributing](https://kirana.style/docs/project/contributing.md): How to report a bug, fix the docs, get a pull request merged, and support Kirana.
- [For LLMs](https://kirana.style/docs/project/llms.md): Plain-text endpoints of this documentation, written for coding agents: llms.txt, the full text, and a markdown twin of every page.
- [Agent skills](https://kirana.style/docs/project/agent-skills.md): Two installable skills teach a coding agent to write Kirana and to migrate to it, with the rules that cause real bugs, the check, trace and report loop, and every diagnostic and lint rule.
